page: Amazon Web Services r6g.large is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by custom 64-bit ARM architecture. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs based on the AWS Graviton2 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture clocked at 2.5 GHz. Each core has access to 64 KB of L1 data cache and 1.0 MB of L2 cache, backed by 32 MB of shared L3 cache with hardware cryptographic acceleration via ARM AES instructions.

The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM allocation ratio (8.0 GB per core). Local storage is absent, meaning workloads require network-attached storage solutions. Networking features a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance includes no GPU acceleration, focusing entirely on memory density.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest raw compute throughput alongside stable caching capabilities. In CPU evaluations, the r6g.large achieved 1,519.48 in stress-ng single-core tests and 3,014.98 in multi-core tests, alongside a Geekbench single-core score of 933.0 and multi-core score of 1,706.0. Memory bandwidth reached 117.04 GB/sec on cached read-only tests and 36.62 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB read blocks. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET operations reached 2.28 million operations per second, while PassMark database operations scored 1,309.06.

Given its ARM-based architecture and substantial memory-to-core ratio, the r6g.large delivers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound tasks that do not demand extreme single-thread or vector compute capabilities. The instance is suited for caching layers, in-memory databases like Redis or Memcached, lightweight transactional relational databases, and data preprocessing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r6g.large is a memory-optimized instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture running at 2.5 GHz under the Nitro System. With 16.0 GB of RAM, the instance delivers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance recorded a stress-ng single-core score of 1,519.48, Geekbench multi-core performance of 1,706.0, and Redis throughput of 2.28 million SET operations per second. Memory throughput reached 117.04 GB/sec for cached reads. Due to its balanced memory capacity and power-efficient Graviton architecture, the r6g.large is well suited for in-memory caches, small-to-midsize relational databases, and memory-dependent microservices.
